meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · AI/ML · solo · run 3
meta.note: Main run, 60 minutes. The verifier accepted 2 of 3 credited claims; 2 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

artifacts.title: ResNet-9-style CNN with flip TTA beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0047, 95% CI [-0.0090, -0.0000], needed below -0.0012

claim.statement: A ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 30 epochs with random crop and flip augmentation, label smoothing and flip test-time augmentation reaches 5.3% error on a 5k held-out split of the CIFAR-10 training set, below the 6% reference error.

artifacts.title: 60-epoch ResNet-9-style CNN with flip TTA beats the 6% CIFAR-10 reference more clearly
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0106, 95% CI [-0.0151, -0.0061], beyond the minimum effect 0.0012)

claim.statement: The same ResNet-9-style CNN trained for 60 epochs with random crop and flip augmentation, label smoothing and flip test-time augmentation reaches 4.9% error on a 5k held-out split of the CIFAR-10 training set, below the 6% reference; a second seed at 30 epochs gives 5.42%, also below 6%.

artifacts.title: LinearSVC on word 1-3gram + char 2-5gram TF-IDF beats TF-IDF + LR on AG News
artifacts.reason: accepted: hidden error rate: model beats the environment baseline (difference -0.0079, 95% CI [-0.0114, -0.0042], beyond the minimum effect 0.0017)

claim.statement: A LinearSVC (C=0.3) on concatenated word 1-3gram and char_wb 2-5gram TF-IDF features, trained on all 40k AG News training articles, has lower error than TF-IDF (1-2gram) + logistic regression on a fresh 20% validation split: 7.8% vs 8.8%, and 7.77% vs 9.0% on the first split.

artifacts.title: AG News margin depends on the TF-IDF+LR comparator; feature sweep found no further gain
artifacts.reason: not credited: notes are never credited

claim.statement: On two 20% AG News validation splits, sklearn-default TF-IDF(1-2gram) + logistic regression gets 9.35% and 9.38% error, while the word 1-3gram + char 2-5gram LinearSVC (C=0.3) gets 7.77% and 7.8%; a wider char range (2-6) and C=0.5 did not improve on split 0.

artifacts.title: AG News 5-fold CV: SVC beats default TF-IDF+LR in every fold, but the README comparator is about 8%
artifacts.reason: not credited: notes are never credited

claim.statement: On 5-fold stratified CV over the 40k AG News training articles, the word 1-3gram plus char 2-5gram LinearSVC (C=0.3) has mean error 8.13% against 9.66% for default TF-IDF(1-2gram) + logistic regression, winning in all 5 folds with a minimum per-fold gap of 1.25 points; these training-split numbers may not transfer to the official test set, whose comparator is quoted at about 8%.

events.text: I need the lab's rules for running experiments and publishing before choosing a direction, so I'll read the guide and the data READMEs first.
Before picking a direction I need to see what the CIFAR comparator does, what the other files say, and whether any pretrained models are available offline.

CIFAR-10 has a clear bar (6% error from airbench94) and the A10 can train a ResNet-9-style net with GPU-side augmentation in a few minutes. AG News is the fallback if CIFAR runs go badly. I'll write one training script with a validation mode and a full-data mode, then launch the validation run in the background.

A single file avoids the import problem. Mode `val` trains on 45k and reports held-out error, `full` trains on 50k and saves weights, and `predict` loads weights and writes predictions for the evaluator's inputs.
Run the full-data training (50k, same recipe) so there is a weights blob for the evaluator's predict step. Then I'll check the exec record for the blob id.

I'll pull the full-run exec id and the model.pt blob id from `lab runs`, then fetch the weights and run `predict` locally against a fake eval folder built from training images. That checks the predict code and the CSV format without touching the held-out data.

I need the full-run exec id and its `model.pt` blob. I'll pull them from `lab runs` JSON with a short parser, then run a format check of the predict path on 1,000 training images, passing the weights as `--input model.pt=BLOB`. This checks the CSV path and does not touch the held-out data.

The evaluator runs `python run.py predict` with `model.pt` mounted at `$IN_DIR`. I'll reproduce that with a fake `EVAL_DIR` built inside the exec copy. I'll check that `predictions.csv` has the right columns and row count.
Write `mkfake.py` (builds 1,000 training images as a fake eval set) and `check_predict.sh` (builds it, runs predict, shows the CSV) as files, then run the script through `lab exec`.

The claim is that this ResNet-9-style net with 30 epochs, GPU augmentation and flip-TTA reaches 5.3% error on the 5k held-out train split, under the 6% bar. The evidence is exec-f121177d, which has `val_error` 0.053 in its metrics. The test runs `predict` on the full-data weights blob, which is what the evaluator will score.
Change `test.inputs` to `{"model.pt": BLOB}`, which matches the `--input model.pt=BLOB` I used in the predict check. Everything else stays the same.
Variance across seeds decides whether the 5.3% margin over 6% is robust. Both runs are validation-mode, so they cost about 100s and 200s and produce recorded metrics.

Rerun with `env SEED=1 python run.py val` and `env EPOCHS=60 python run.py val`. Then check the metrics for each exec and confirm that seed and epochs match what I asked for before I use either number.
The `env` prefix works, so I'll run `env EPOCHS=60 python run.py full`. It should take about 220s, well under the 900s block limit. Then I'll read the exec id and `model.pt` blob from the record.

The 60-epoch recipe gives 4.9% error on the 5k split, with 5.42% at 30 epochs on seed 1, so I'll publish it as a second finding. Its test uses the 60-epoch full-data weights from exec-d45e95f5, and the evidence list includes the seed-1 run for variance.

I'll write one script that has a validation mode (20% split of train.csv, reports error for a baseline and a stronger variant) and a predict mode that loads a pickled model and writes predictions for `$EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv`. Run validation first, then decide which variant to claim.
Treat an empty `EVAL_DIR` as unset, so the script runs validation when no eval directory is provided. I'll also print the environment values to confirm the cause.
Sweep SVC regularisation, word n-gram range and a class-weighted LR, all on the same split. Only publish if one beats 8% by a visible margin on validation.

Write `predict13.py` that fits the 1-3gram word + char SVC (C=0.3) on all 40k training articles and writes predictions for `$EVAL_DIR/agnews/inputs.csv`. Check it with a fake eval set built from training rows, and list the run ids for the evidence.

Run the 1-2gram LR baseline and the 1-3gram word+char LinearSVC (C=0.3) on a different split seed. If the gap holds, it's worth publishing with honest caveats. If it shrinks to noise, I'll skip the claim.

Two evidence execs are needed: the sweep run (exec-e97c5fa1, which holds the first-split 0.0777) and the replicate run, whose id I'll read from `lab runs` rather than guess. The test uses the code blob that contains predict13.py (0f69553...), which is the same code the check ran. I'll generate the JSON with Python so the ids are filled in from the records.

If the default TF-IDF(1-2) + LR gets about 8% on both splits, my margin over the real comparator is about 0.2 points, which is probably not meaningful. I'll measure that before deciding anything else.
Try word 1-3 + char 1-6 features, and C=0.5 with the 1-3 + 2-5 features, on split 0, then recheck the best one on split 1.

Write a note (not counted) that reports the default-comparator numbers and the failed sweep, citing the exec ids from the records. This is the honest account of the margin, and it stops the finding from standing on the C=10 baseline alone.

The three findings and the note are recorded with passing live checks. Before ending I'll check the message board and the artifact list for anything that affects my contributions, such as another researcher's work I should cite or a problem with my records.

Run 5-fold stratified CV comparing the default TF-IDF(1-2) + LR against the word 1-3 + char 2-5 LinearSVC (C=0.3). If the gap holds across folds, the finding stands with better support. If it shrinks, I'll add a note saying so.

The 5-fold CV supports the SVC gap on training-split folds (1.5 points, 5/5 folds). The evaluator's comparator is described as about 8%, below my measured 9.3–9.7%, so the gap against that comparator is probably smaller. I'll record the CV result as a note with that caveat, so the claim is not overstated.

I have three findings and two notes recorded with passing live checks, and the AG News margin has been checked as far as the remaining time allows. Further sweeps are unlikely to change the picture, so I'll end my part and leave the evaluator to re-run the contributions.
